prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A small antenna includes: a first element having a pair of conductors with a power feeding point; and a second element as a conductor arranged to sandwich a dielectric body. A part of the first and second elements has an inductance shape. A first resonance mode with a same current direction of the first element as the second element has a first resonant frequency. A second resonance mode with an opposite current direction of the first element to the second element has a second resonant frequency. A length from each power feeding point to the inductance shape is determined to hold the first resonant frequency within a range from a frequency slightly higher than the second resonant frequency to a high anti-resonant frequency of the second resonance mode, or a range from a frequency slightly lower than the second resonant frequency to a low anti-resonant frequency of the resonance mode.

outputs.L1: A small antenna includes a first element comprising a pair of conductors having a power-feeding point, and a second element comprising a conductor arranged to sandwich a dielectric body. A portion of each of the first and second elements has an inductive shape. A first resonance mode, in which current flows in the same direction through the first and second elements, has a first resonant frequency. A second resonance mode, in which current flows in opposite directions through the first and second elements, has a second resonant frequency. The length from each power-feeding point to the inductive shape is selected such that the first resonant frequency falls within either a range extending from a frequency slightly higher than the second resonant frequency to a high anti-resonant frequency of the second resonance mode, or a range extending from a frequency slightly lower than the second resonant frequency to a low anti-resonant frequency of the resonance mode.
outputs.L2: A compact antenna comprises a first element formed by two conductors, each provided with a power-feed point, and a second conductive element positioned so that the two elements enclose a dielectric body. Portions of both elements are configured as inductive structures. In a first resonant mode, current flows in the same direction through the first and second elements, producing a first resonant frequency. In a second resonant mode, currents in the two elements flow in opposite directions, producing a second resonant frequency. The distance between each power-feed point and the inductive structure is selected so that the first resonant frequency lies either between a frequency slightly above the second resonant frequency and the upper anti-resonant frequency of the second mode, or between a frequency slightly below the second resonant frequency and the lower anti-resonant frequency of that mode.
outputs.L3:
The small antenna includes a first element formed by a pair of conductors, each having a power-feeding point. A second conductive element is arranged opposite the first element, with a dielectric body sandwiched between the first and second elements. At least a portion of each element has an inductive shape that provides a desired inductance.

The antenna supports two resonance modes. In the first resonance mode, currents flowing through the first and second elements travel in the same direction. In the second resonance mode, the currents flow in opposite directions. The distance from each power-feeding point to the corresponding inductive portion is selected so that the first resonant frequency is positioned close to the second resonant frequency. In addition, the first resonant frequency is set within a specified anti-resonant frequency range, thereby enabling the compact antenna to achieve the desired resonance characteristics.
outputs.L4:
A compact multi-resonant antenna includes a pair of fed conductors and an additional conductor arranged on opposite sides of a dielectric layer. The conductors cooperate electromagnetically through the dielectric, forming a compact stacked or sandwich structure. Inductive sections are provided at selected positions along the conductors to modify the electrical path length and the current distribution without requiring a corresponding increase in the antenna’s physical dimensions.

The arrangement supports at least two characteristic current modes. In one mode, currents on the coupled conductors flow substantially in the same direction. In another mode, the currents flow substantially in opposite directions. Each mode produces a different resonance, while the interaction between the conductors can also create an anti-resonance adjacent to one of those resonances. The inductive sections are positioned and dimensioned so that these modal frequencies can be controlled with a useful degree of independence.

In particular, the distance from the feed point to an inductive section is selected to place the first resonant frequency close to the second resonant frequency. Preferably, the first resonance is located within the frequency range associated with the anti-resonance adjacent to the second resonance. This relationship alters the input-impedance response so that the resonances interact constructively rather than appearing as widely separated or poorly matched operating points.

By adjusting the feed-to-inductance length, the inductance values, conductor dimensions, conductor spacing, and dielectric properties, the antenna can be tuned to provide multiple closely spaced resonances or a broader combined operating band. The resulting structure achieves effective impedance matching and multi-frequency operation while remaining physically compact, making it suitable for space-constrained wireless devices and other applications requiring a low-profile antenna.
outputs.L5: A small antenna stood on the roof, thin and almost invisible against the sky. Though modest in size, it connected the house to voices, music, and news from faraway places. In rain, wind, and sunlight, it remained steady, quietly receiving signals that traveled across cities and fields. It was a simple device with an important task—a tiny bridge between the home and the wider world.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the key technical features of a compact dual-resonance antenna, including its conductors, dielectric body, inductance shape, and resonant-frequency relationship.
counterfactuals.output:
- **Conductors:** Two electrically coupled conductive elements of different effective lengths provide two resonant modes, typically sharing a feed or ground connection.  
- **Dielectric body:** The conductors are formed on or around a compact high-permittivity dielectric body, which electrically lengthens the antenna and reduces its physical size.  
- **Inductive section:** At least one conductor includes a folded, helical, or meander-shaped inductance section, increasing current-path length and lowering resonance without enlarging the antenna.  
- **Dual resonance:** The two conductor paths produce lower and upper resonant frequencies; the upper resonance is designed to be approximately twice the lower resonance, enabling operation in two related frequency bands.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a small antenna having first and second elements that support same-direction and opposite-direction current resonance modes.
counterfactuals.output: A compact antenna includes first and second conductive antenna elements disposed adjacent to one another and coupled to a feed structure. The antenna elements are configured to support a first resonance mode in which currents on the first and second antenna elements flow in substantially the same direction and a second resonance mode in which currents on the first and second antenna elements flow in substantially opposite directions. Dimensions, spacing, and coupling of the antenna elements are selected to establish respective resonant frequencies for the first and second resonance modes. Excitation of the resonance modes enables the antenna to operate over multiple frequency bands or an increased operating bandwidth while occupying a reduced physical volume. In some implementations, one or more reactive, dielectric, or tuning structures are coupled to the antenna elements to adjust the resonant frequencies, impedance matching, or radiation characteristics of the antenna.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain how the distance from the feeding points to the inductive portion is selected to control the first resonant frequency relative to the second resonance mode and its anti-resonant frequencies.
counterfactuals.output:
The spacing is chosen as an **electrical distance**, not merely a physical dimension. The conductor section between each feed point and the inductive portion contributes phase delay and distributed capacitance. Together with the inductance, it determines the input reactance and therefore the first-mode resonance.

Design proceeds as follows:

1. Determine the second mode’s resonant frequency and the anti-resonant frequencies on either side of it from the input-impedance response.
2. Adjust the feed-to-inductive-section distance until the first mode’s reactance crosses zero at the desired frequency relative to those points—typically within the frequency interval bounded by the relevant anti-resonances, so the two modes can form a usable matched band.
3. Verify that the resistance at the resulting resonance is suitable for feeding.

Increasing the distance increases the effective electrical length and generally shifts the first resonance downward; decreasing it shifts that resonance upward. The second mode and its anti-resonances are usually less sensitive to this distance, so they serve as reference points for positioning the first resonance. In practice, the final distance is found using an impedance/eigenmode simulation because bends, substrate permittivity, coupling, and fringing fields alter the simple transmission-line estimate.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
